result.markdown: --- title: "Integration" subtitle: "Definite integrals from samples" engine: julia --- Integrals of sampled data, on uniform grids in one to three dimensions and from scattered points in 2D. The convolution interpolant's antiderivative is built once and a box integral is then four (or eight) evaluations by inclusion–exclusion; the alternatives are quadrature rules on the samples (NumericalIntegration.jl), and the exact integrals of spline interpolants (BSplineKit.jl, Dierckx.jl), applied along one axis at a time in more dimensions. For scattered points the comparison is a thin-plate radial basis interpolant integrated by adaptive cubature, since no package integrates scattered data directly. ::: {#2 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="Packages, the methods, and the test integrands"} using ConvolutionInterpolations using NumericalIntegration # integrate(x, y, rule): Trapezoidal, SimpsonEven, RombergEven using BSplineKit # interpolate(x, y, BSplineOrder(k)) and integral(spline) import Dierckx # qualified: Dierckx also exports `integrate` import ScatteredInterpolation # qualified: also exports `interpolate` using HCubature, QuadGK # reference integrals, and integration of the RBF interpolant using Chairmarks, Printf, Random, CairoMakie # 1D rules: each maps (x, y) on a uniform grid to the definite integral over [x[1], x[end]] trap_rule(x, y) = integrate(x, y, Trapezoidal()) # 2nd order simpson_rule(x, y) = integrate(x, y, SimpsonEven()) # 4th order romberg_rule(x, y) = Base.CoreLogging.with_logger(Base.CoreLogging.NullLogger()) do # its convergence warnings are not the point here integrate(x, y, RombergEven()) # high order, needs n = 2^k + 1 points end function bspline_rule(k) # order-k B-spline interpolant, exact spline integral return (x, y) -> begin S = BSplineKit.interpolate(x, y, BSplineOrder(k)) I = integral(S) return I(last(x)) - I(first(x)) end end function dierckx_rule(x, y) # FITPACK quintic spline, exact spline integral spl = Dierckx.Spline1D(collect(x), collect(y); k = 5, s = 0.0) return Dierckx.integrate(spl, first(x), last(x)) end # a 1D rule lifted to N-D by integrating along one axis at a time function nested_integral(rule, axes::NTuple{N,<:AbstractVector}, A::AbstractArray{T,N}) where {T,N} B = A for d in N:-1:1 x = axes[d] B = mapslices(v -> rule(x, v), B; dims = d) # integrate every line along axis d B = dropdims(B; dims = d) # that axis is gone now end return B[] # 0-dimensional array -> scalar end function conv_query(F, lo, hi) # the integral over the box [lo, hi] N = length(lo) total = 0.0 for corner in Iterators.product(ntuple(_ -> (false, true), N)...) pt = ntuple(d -> corner[d] ? hi[d] : lo[d], N) sgn = isodd(N - count(corner)) ? -1.0 : 1.0 total += sgn * F(pt...) end return total end # the convolution interpolant: the iterated antiderivative once, then inclusion–exclusion over the corners function conv_box_integral(axes::NTuple{N,<:AbstractVector}, A::AbstractArray{T,N}; kernel = :b7) where {T,N} grid = N == 1 ? axes[1] : axes F = convolution_interpolation(grid, A; kernel = kernel, derivative = -1) return conv_query(F, first.(axes), last.(axes)) end methods = [ "Trapezoid" => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(trap_rule, axes, A), "Simpson" => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(simpson_rule, axes, A), "Romberg" => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(romberg_rule, axes, A), "Dierckx k=5" => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(dierckx_rule, axes, A), "BSplineKit k=4" => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(bspline_rule(4), axes, A), "BSplineKit k=8" => (axes, A) -> nested_integral(bspline_rule(8), axes, A), "ConvInterp :b7" => (axes, A) -> conv_box_integral(axes, A; kernel = :b7), "ConvInterp :b13" => (axes, A) -> conv_box_integral(axes, A; kernel = :b13), ] # the test integrands and their reference integrals g(x) = exp(x) * cos(4x) + 1 / (1 + 16 * (x - 0.4)^2) # smooth, non-polynomial, non-periodic I_g = quadgk(g, 0.0, 1.0; rtol = 1e-14)[1] # 1D reference f_sep(p...) = prod(g, p) # separable N-D integrand, reference I_g^N f2(x, y) = exp(-3 * (x - 0.4)^2 - 2 * (y - 0.6)^2) * cos(4 * x * y + y) # non-separable 2D integrand I_f2 = hcubature(p -> f2(p[1], p[2]), [0.0, 0.0], [1.0, 1.0]; rtol = 1e-13)[1]; ``` ::: The integrands are $g(x) = e^x \cos 4x + 1/(1 + 16(x - 0.4)^2)$, products of it in more dimensions, and a non-separable Gaussian-times-cosine in 2D; the references come from adaptive quadrature at tolerance $10^{-13}$ and below. ## Convergence The relative error of each method against the number of points per axis, on grids of $2^k + 1$ points so that Romberg's rule applies: ::: {#4 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="The convergence study"} function run_uniform(N, ns, methods, f, I_ref) errs = Dict(name => Float64[] for name in first.(methods)) for n in ns axes = ntuple(_ -> range(0.0, 1.0; length = n), N) A = [f(p...) for p in Iterators.product(axes...)] for (name, m) in methods push!(errs[name], abs(m(axes, A) - I_ref) / abs(I_ref)) end end return errs end ns_1d = [9, 17, 33, 65, 129, 257] ns_2d = [9, 17, 33, 65, 129] ns_3d = [9, 17, 33, 65] # 65³ = 274 625 samples, the most expensive case errs_1d = run_uniform(1, ns_1d, methods, f_sep, I_g^1) errs_2d = run_uniform(2, ns_2d, methods, f_sep, I_g^2) errs_3d = run_uniform(3, ns_3d, methods, f_sep, I_g^3) errs_2n = run_uniform(2, ns_2d, methods, f2, I_f2) cases = [("1D, separable", ns_1d, errs_1d), ("2D, separable", ns_2d, errs_2d), ("3D, separable", ns_3d, errs_3d), ("2D, non-separable", ns_2d, errs_2n)] fig = Figure(size = (800, 1200)) for (i, (title, ns, errs)) in enumerate(cases) ax = Axis(fig[i, 1]; xscale = log10, yscale = log10, title = title, xlabel = "points per axis", ylabel = "relative error") for (name, _) in methods scatterlines!(ax, ns, max.(errs[name], 1e-17); markersize = 8, label = name) end Legend(fig[i, 2], ax) end fig ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: | Observed order | 1D | 2D | 3D | 2D non-separable | |:--|--:|--:|--:|--:| | Trapezoid | 2.00 | 2.00 | 2.00 | 2.00 | | Simpson | 4.34 | 4.48 | 4.61 | 4.28 | | Romberg | 9.45 | 7.85 | 6.05 | 10.67 | | Dierckx k=5 | 6.80 | 7.55 | 7.93 | 7.14 | | BSplineKit k=4 | 5.44 | 5.14 | 5.01 | 6.45 | | BSplineKit k=8 | 5.71 | 9.23 | 8.47 | 7.34 | | ConvInterp :b7 | 5.61 | 8.99 | 4.72 | 8.10 | | ConvInterp :b13 | 5.24 | 9.08 | 6.40 | 8.22 | An order near zero on the finest grids means the method has reached rounding, not that it has stopped converging; the curves show which. ## Scattered points Points scattered in the unit square, the non-separable integrand sampled at them without noise, and the integral over the points' bounding box. The convolution route is the exact scattered fit with `derivative = -1`, which gives the antiderivative interpolant directly; the alternative is a thin-plate radial basis interpolant integrated by adaptive cubature, which costs a dense solve and one interpolant evaluation per cubature point: ::: {#8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="The scattered-data comparison"} function scattered_comparison(f, n_list; seed = 1) rng = MersenneTwister(seed) rows = NamedTuple[] for npts in n_list pts = rand(rng, 2, npts) # columns are points in [0, 1]² vals = [f(pts[1, i], pts[2, i]) for i in 1:npts] lo = [minimum(pts[1, :]), minimum(pts[2, :])] hi = [maximum(pts[1, :]), maximum(pts[2, :])] I_ref = hcubature(p -> f(p[1], p[2]), lo, hi; rtol = 1e-13)[1] t0 = time_ns() F = convolution_interpolation(pts, vals; mode = :exact, derivative = -1) I_conv = conv_query(F, lo, hi) t_conv = (time_ns() - t0) / 1e9 t0 = time_ns() rbf = ScatteredInterpolation.interpolate(ScatteredInterpolation.ThinPlate(), pts, vals) I_rbf = hcubature(p -> ScatteredInterpolation.evaluate(rbf, reshape(p, 2, 1))[1], lo, hi; rtol = 1e-10, maxevals = 500_000)[1] t_rbf = (time_ns() - t0) / 1e9 push!(rows, (n = npts, e_conv = abs(I_conv - I_ref) / abs(I_ref), t_conv = t_conv, e_rbf = abs(I_rbf - I_ref) / abs(I_ref), t_rbf = t_rbf)) end return rows end scattered_rows = scattered_comparison(f2, [500, 1000, 2000]); ``` ::: | points | ConvInterp error | ConvInterp time | thin-plate RBF + cubature error | RBF time | |--:|--:|--:|--:|--:| | 500 | 2.3e-06 | 3.28 s | 1.1e-04 | 3.72 s | | 1000 | 2.2e-07 | 0.41 s | 4.8e-05 | 6.25 s | | 2000 | 4.6e-08 | 0.65 s | 6.6e-05 | 11.48 s | ## Setup and query The antiderivative interpolant is built once; after that a definite integral over any sub-box is a few evaluations, independent of the grid size. Of the alternatives, BSplineKit (1D) and Dierckx's `Spline2D` (2D) have a comparable split between setup and query; the quadrature rules have no reusable setup, and integrate grid-aligned boxes only. ::: {#12 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.julia .cell-code code-fold="true" code-summary="The timings"} function timing_rows(N, ns, f; kernel = :b7) rng = MersenneTwister(2) rows = NamedTuple[] for n in ns axes = ntuple(_ -> range(0.0, 1.0; length = n), N) A = [f(p...) for p in Iterators.product(axes...)] grid = N == 1 ? axes[1] : axes lo = ntuple(_ -> 0.1 + 0.3 * rand(rng), N) # one random sub-box, shared by every method hi = ntuple(_ -> 0.6 + 0.3 * rand(rng), N) t_setup = (@b convolution_interpolation($grid, $A; kernel = $kernel, derivative = -1)).time F = convolution_interpolation(grid, A; kernel = kernel, derivative = -1) t_query = (@b conv_query($F, $lo, $hi)).time t_s = t_q = NaN if N == 1 x = axes[1] t_s = (@b integral(BSplineKit.interpolate($x, $A, BSplineOrder(8)))).time I = integral(BSplineKit.interpolate(x, A, BSplineOrder(8))) t_q = (@b $I($(hi[1])) - $I($(lo[1]))).time elseif N == 2 x, y = collect(axes[1]), collect(axes[2]) t_s = (@b Dierckx.Spline2D($x, $y, $A; kx = 5, ky = 5, s = 0.0)).time spl = Dierckx.Spline2D(x, y, A; kx = 5, ky = 5, s = 0.0) t_q = (@b Dierckx.integrate($spl, $(lo[1]), $(hi[1]), $(lo[2]), $(hi[2]))).time end push!(rows, (n = n, t_setup = t_setup, t_query = t_query, t_s = t_s, t_q = t_q)) end return rows end timings = [(1, "BSplineKit k=8", timing_rows(1, ns_1d, f_sep)), (2, "Dierckx k=5", timing_rows(2, ns_2d, f_sep)), (3, "", timing_rows(3, ns_3d, f_sep))]; ``` ::: **1D**, kernel `:b7` against BSplineKit k=8 | points per axis | ConvInterp setup | ConvInterp query | BSplineKit k=8 setup | BSplineKit k=8 query | |--:|--:|--:|--:|--:| | 9 | 6.1 μs | 57 ns | 623 ns | 37 ns | | 17 | 6.2 μs | 41 ns | 1.7 μs | 39 ns | | 33 | 6.2 μs | 41 ns | 2.6 μs | 39 ns | | 65 | 6.5 μs | 32 ns | 5.2 μs | 40 ns | | 129 | 6.8 μs | 32 ns | 10.4 μs | 42 ns | | 257 | 7.7 μs | 32 ns | 21.3 μs | 44 ns | **2D**, kernel `:b7` against Dierckx k=5 | points per axis | ConvInterp setup | ConvInterp query | Dierckx k=5 setup | Dierckx k=5 query | |--:|--:|--:|--:|--:| | 9 | 22.5 μs | 337 ns | 4.7 μs | 282 ns | | 17 | 28.5 μs | 302 ns | 13.4 μs | 351 ns | | 33 | 42.1 μs | 281 ns | 45.3 μs | 431 ns | | 65 | 83.4 μs | 257 ns | 165.9 μs | 1.2 μs | | 129 | 205.3 μs | 257 ns | 635.3 μs | 3.3 μs | **3D**, kernel `:b7` (no competitor with a reusable setup) | points per axis | ConvInterp setup | ConvInterp query | | | |--:|--:|--:|--:|--:| | 9 | 329.2 μs | 4.5 μs | — | — | | 17 | 734.1 μs | 4.4 μs | — | — | | 33 | 2.28 ms | 4.4 μs | — | — | | 65 | 12.61 ms | 4.3 μs | — | — | The query column is the point: once the interpolant exists, an integral over any box costs microseconds whatever the grid, in any dimension. The setup grows with the grid, as any interpolant's does, and the 3D rows show it is still the only route with a reusable setup there.
